title: Bacchus
source: Uffizi Gallery, Florence (public domain). Full resolution from Wikimedia Commons: Bacchus-Caravaggio_(1595).jpg
caption: The god of wine, offering you a glass. Look into the wine flask on the left: Caravaggio may have painted himself there, at work. #art #arthistory #painting #history #oilpainting

slides.headline: Caravaggio hid a tiny self-portrait in this painting
Look at the wine flask
slides.text: Bottom left, a glass flask of red wine. On its surface, a tiny reflection that went unnoticed for centuries.

slides.headline: The painter, at work
slides.text: Cleaning and modern imaging revealed a small figure at an easel reflected in the glass. Many believe it is Caravaggio painting this very picture.

slides.headline: The fruit is going bad
slides.text: Look at the bowl: bruised, split and overripe fruit. Pleasure doesn't last, a common message in paintings of the time.

slides.headline: A worm hole
slides.text: Even the apple has a hole in it. Caravaggio painted decay as carefully as beauty.

slides.headline: Dirty fingernails
slides.text: The god of wine has dirt under his nails. Caravaggio painted real people from the street, not idealised gods.

slides.headline: The wine is moving
slides.text: Small ripples on the surface of the wine in his glass, as if he has just lifted it towards you.

slides.headline: Flushed cheeks
slides.text: Red cheeks, heavy eyes, a slightly tired look. This Bacchus has already had a few glasses.

slides.headline: An invitation
slides.text: With his other hand he plays with the black ribbon holding his robe. The whole painting is an offer: a drink, and maybe more.
